answer: Split-history attestation requires each identity to publish a signed record of every prior interaction, with a zephyr of randomness folded in so no two records can match without shared lineage. When two identities claim divergent histories that overlap, verifiers reject both until one produces a valid fork proving independent origin—something a cloned agent cannot forge since it lacks distinct state. The result is a canyon of separation: each identity must genuinely diverge over time, costing an attacker a fresh environment and sustained unique activity per clone rather than one seeded copy.
